difficultyRationale: Probes whether a candidate understands that 'exactly-once' is a property of carefully-combined mechanisms, not a single transport-level switch.
prompt: A developer sets Kafka's idempotent producer (`enable.idempotence=true`) and transactional APIs, and tells the team "we now have exactly-once delivery end to end." A reviewer pushes back, saying that claim is too broad as stated. What is the reviewer's objection?
explanation: Kafka's idempotent producer and transactions give exactly-once semantics for writes *within Kafka itself* — a producer won't create duplicate records on retry, and a consume-process-produce chain can be made atomic via transactions. But "exactly-once" for the whole pipeline also depends on what happens outside Kafka: if the consumer's processing has an external side effect (a database write, an email, a call to another service) that isn't itself transactionally tied to the offset commit, that external effect can still happen more than once on redelivery. End-to-end exactly-once requires either making that external effect idempotent or wrapping it and the offset commit in the same atomic unit (e.g., a transactional outbox) — Kafka's own guarantee alone doesn't cover it.

options.text: Kafka's idempotent producer and transactions only guarantee exactly-once semantics for writes inside Kafka; an external side effect outside that boundary can still be duplicated on redelivery unless it's made idempotent or tied into the same atomic unit.
options.explanation: Correct. This is exactly the scope Kafka documents for its exactly-once semantics: it covers producer retries and Kafka-to-Kafka transactional pipelines, not arbitrary external effects a consumer triggers as part of processing a message.

options.text: The reviewer is objecting that `enable.idempotence=true` by itself does nothing without also setting `acks=all`, so the producer is still at risk of silently dropping records on a leader failure regardless of any transactional configuration.
options.explanation: Kafka's idempotent producer actually requires `acks=all` as a precondition and enforces it (overriding a lower setting), so this isn't the gap in the developer's claim — the real gap is about effects outside Kafka's own transactional boundary, not about `acks`.

options.text: The reviewer is pointing out that transactions in Kafka only apply to the producer side, so a consumer reading from a transactional topic will still see uncommitted, in-flight records mixed in with committed ones unless it polls with a special flag.
options.explanation: Kafka's read-committed isolation level (the consumer-side counterpart to producer transactions) exists precisely to filter out uncommitted records for a consumer that opts into it; this isn't the gap being raised about end-to-end external side effects.

options.text: The reviewer means that idempotent producers only protect against network-level retries of the exact same request, but a completely separate retry triggered manually by an operator would still produce a duplicate record regardless of any producer configuration.
options.explanation: Kafka's idempotent producer de-duplicates based on a sequence number per producer session tied to the broker, which also covers a fresh retry attempt sent by the same producer instance, not only an automatic low-level network retry; this isn't the specific gap the reviewer is raising about effects outside Kafka.

references.title: Confluent Documentation — Kafka Delivery Semantics (exactly-once's external-system caveat: systems claiming it "may not account for cases where a consumer or producer outside of the system has failed")
